newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB to dispose of 550 bln yen in problem loans.
newsitem.headline: DKB to dispose of 550 bln yen in problem loans.

text.p: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, a major Japanese commercial bank, said on Friday that it would dispose of 550 billion yen worth of problem loans in the current 1996/97 business year ending on March 31.
The bank also said in a statement that it would shed 3,000 employees over four years from 1996/97 in order to cut costs.
It is also planning to merge or close more than 30 domestic offices in four years from 1996/97, it said.
Out of the total 550 billion yen problem loan disposals, 250 billion yen would be taxable, it said.
The bank also said 200 billion yen of the total problem loan disposal would be aimed at writing off financial support it provided to three financial affiliates.

Dai-Ichi Kangyo (DKB) said in the statement it decided to drastically dispose of problem loans in 1996/97 because it is important to solve its problem loans as early as possible to cope with "the new financial era".
DKB said it would write off problem loans in 1996/97 as much as possible for now, taking account of a protracted economic slump and falling real estate prices.

DKB earlier said that by disposing of such a huge amount of problem loans it expects a parent current loss of 300 billion yen in 1996/97 against its earlier forecast of a 40 billion yen profit and an actual 129.67 billion yen in profit in 1995/96.
